text:
maya: @acme-inc-support - heads up, customer reports ~48h of missing audit events in their SIEM after we rolled the retention TTL change yesterday. They see gaps for tenant 6789. sample ids: evt-20260301-99, evt-20260302-04, evt-20260302-08. They say the collector rejected payloads with 'schema: missing actor.id'.

acme-inc-support: Correct - our SIEM shows 142 blobs rejected between 2026-03-01T20:00Z and 2026-03-02T12:30Z. We tried one raw gz and got parse error.

siem-bot: alert: forwarder-delivery-failure tenant=6789 reason=schema_mismatch count=142 last_attempt=2026-03-02T14:12:03Z

alex: Thanks Maya. Two quick asks: (1) can you paste the manifest S3 keys for that window, (2) include a short hexdump/header of one of the gz payloads? Also did a KMS alias rotation or vault rekey overlap the TTL change?

maya: Manifest keys below (masked):
```
s3://audit-exports/tenant-6789/2026-03-01/manifest-20260301-1.json
s3://audit-exports/tenant-6789/2026-03-01/manifest-20260301-2.json
s3://audit-exports/tenant-6789/2026-03-02/manifest-20260302-1.json
```
Example gzip header from one rejected blob (first 64 bytes):
```
1f 8b 08 00 00 00 00 00 00 03 7b 22 65 76 74 5f 69 64 22 3a 22 65 76 74 2d 32 30 32 36 30 33 30 31 2d 39 39 22 2c 22 61 63 74 6f 72 22 3a 7b 7d
```
Looks like actor field is "{}" in some events. We did a TTL policy rollout at 2026-03-01T19:50Z and changed default retention from 90d->45d for test tenants.

chloe: My suspicion: the TTL cutoff was shifted backwards during the config flip and our forwarder marked older events as 'tombstones' then applied redaction (strip identity fields) to comply with new retention. The SIEM's ingestion rejects events missing actor.id. So the events aren't "missing" from S3, they're being emitted but redacted and dropped by the customer's collector.

chloe: Short repro/playbook suggestion:
1) identify candidate manifest entries and download the gz (small subset)
2) run our forwarder locally in --allow-old-events mode to re-emit without redaction OR rewrap the blobs with identity unstripped and reupload to a replay location
3) have customer point their collector at replay location to verify acceptance.

chloe: Commands we typically run:
```
# list keys in window
aws s3 ls s3://audit-exports/tenant-6789/2026-03-01/ --recursive | grep manifest

# fetch sample blob
aws s3 cp s3://audit-exports/tenant-6789/2026-03-01/blobs/part-0003.gz - | gunzip -c | head -c 500

# run forwarder locally (example)
./forwarder --manifest manifest-20260301-1.json --allow-old-events --no-redact --target replay-bucket/tenant-6789/test-replay/
```

alex: Also check KMS logs for alias rotation window:
```
# find key events
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=RotateKey
# or grep our key rotation logs
grep -i "alias/tenant-6789" /var/log/kms-rotation.log
```
If the blobs were rewrapped with a new alias and the forwarder didn't include KeyId metadata, customer collector might see a content mismatch too.

maya: I'm going to pull a concrete manifest and run the local forwarder test now. Uploading manifest excerpt in thread.

acme-inc-support: We can validate quickly. If you give us three event ids we can watch the collector real-time.

chloe: Use evt-20260302-04, evt-20260302-08, evt-20260301-99. After re-emitting without redaction they should ingest. If they still fail, collect the collector debug log showing 'schema: missing actor.id' and the raw event body.

alex: I'm going to open an internal incident and assign to eng-security (me) + support (maya). Adding playbook link: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/audit-replay (internal). Also flag SLA P1 for customer.

siem-bot: replay-queue-created id=playback-2765432100-1 eta=2h

maya: Running the forwarder in --allow-old-events now on a small subset. Will post results in ~30m. Scheduling a call with ACME in 1h.

acme-inc-support: Ready for test. We'll switch collector endpoint when you give us the replay URL.

alex: If local re-emission proves successful, plan = (A) run controlled backfill to replay-replay-bucket/tenant-6789/2026-03-01/ (B) adjust forwarder config to not strip actor.* during TTL transitions (short-term), (C) add a guard to our rollout to delay tombstone redaction for 24h after config flips. I'll draft change and post RFC.

chloe: One more note: If KMS rewrap happened, we may need to re-encrypt with customer's collector-compatible key (or provide temporary presigned decrypted copies for SIEM). Coordinate with security ops for key handling.

maya: Updated: local forwarder emitted those three events unchanged and ACME accepted them on their collector. Replaying 10 more blobs now. Will update once the 142 rejected blobs are replayed.

acme-inc-support: We see the three events and their actor.id present, thank you. Waiting on the larger replay.

alex: Great. Assigning follow-ups: chloe will own replay execution; maya will coordinate customer verification; I will own the postmortem and rollout guard. Escalate if replay fails.

siem-bot: incident-created id=INC-2765432100 severity=P1 assignees=alex,chloe,maya

maya: tagging for visibility @eng-oncall @eng-security. Thanks team.
